text: There was a man here. <break time="0.8s" /> Named Jim Smiley. <break time="0.8s" /> In the winter of 1849. <break time="0.8s" /> Or maybe the spring of 1850. <break time="0.8s" /> Wheeler began. <break time="0.8s" /> Smiley was the strangest man. <break time="0.8s" /> I ever saw. <break time="0.8s" /> Because he would bet on anything. <break time="0.8s" /> That came up. <break time="0.8s" /> If he could not find anyone. <break time="0.8s" /> To bet on the other side. <break time="0.8s" /> He would gladly change sides. <break time="0.8s" /> He was lucky, too. <break time="0.8s" /> So lucky that he almost always came out the winner. <break time="0.8s" /> He bet on horse races and dog fights. <break time="0.8s" /> And even on which of two birds. <break time="0.8s" /> On a fence. <break time="0.8s" /> Would fly first. <break time="0.8s" /> If he saw a bug. <break time="0.8s" /> Start to go somewhere. <break time="0.8s" /> He would bet on how long. <break time="0.8s" /> It would take to get there. <break time="0.8s" /> Once Parson Walkers wife was very sick. <break time="0.8s" /> And for a long time it seemed. <break time="0.8s" /> That nobody could save her. <break time="0.8s" /> When the parson said. <break time="0.8s" /> She was much better. <break time="0.8s" /> Smiley answered without thinking. <break time="0.8s" /> Well, I will bet two and a half dollars. <break time="0.8s" /> She does not get well. <break time="0.8s" /> Smiley also had a slow, sickly old mare. <break time="0.8s" /> But he used to win money on her. <break time="0.8s" /> All the same. <break time="0.8s" /> Falling far behind at the start. <break time="0.8s" /> She would get excited. <break time="0.8s" /> Near the end. <break time="0.8s" /> And win by a neck.
